newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SNORAS BANK SEES 96 PROFIT AT 13 MLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: SNORAS BANK SEES 96 PROFIT AT 13 MLN LITAS.

text.p: Lithuania's Snoras Bank's deputy chairman Alexander Churnov said on Friday that it expected its 1996 net profit to be 13 million litas versus just over one million litas in 1995.
"We expect that our 1996 net profit will be 13 million litas," Churnov told Reuters in an interview.
"We had originally planned a net profit of five million litas in 1996," he added.
He also said that the bank intended to boost its share capital this year to meet the central bank's minimum requirement of five million ECU.
The bank's share capital currently stands at 20 million litas.
Churnov said that the bank's strong profits were the result of its activities in the Russian debt market.
"It was a fantastic year for Russian T-bills," he said.
He added that the bank was scanning other lucrative debt opportunities including Ukraine.
The bank is also very active in the soft currency trading market, with a daily turnover of $7 million in this area, he said.
He added that the bank planned to rapidly expand its retail operations.
"We have issued about 10,000 electronic banking cards and plan this year to increase that number to 100,000," he said.
